title: Regression triage notebook and synthetic benchmarks for kernel-selector oscillation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Following the scheduler heuristic change rolled 2025-02-10 we observed a reproducible performance regression on a subset of workloads: intermittent p95/p99 spikes and throughput drops when sequence length distribution includes mixed short and long requests. The failure mode manifests as rapid kernel-selector oscillation ("switchback") where requests flip between two kernel implementations repeatedly within a single session, causing KV-cache misalignment and eviction churn. This ticket creates a reproducible triage notebook, a battery of synthetic benchmarks, and a follow-up action list to harden the selector and CI coverage.
steps_to_reproduce: Checkout runtime@main at commit that landed scheduler heuristic (linked in links).
Observe p95 tail with --probe-window=100ms; enable DEBUG logs for kernel_selector and scheduler to capture oscillation traces.
Replay captured kernel-selection trace against previous stable binary to confirm regression is introduced by selector changes, not model binary.
synthetic_bench_plan: Serpentine generator: interleave short (<=16) and long (>=512) sequences to amplify selector instability.
Sequence-length sweep: run 1k iterations per length bucket and collect per-kernel p50/p95/p99 and cache-hit ratio.
Quant matrix: test fp16, static int8, dynamic int8 with same seeds to identify quant-specific kernel routing defects.
Scheduler probe variables: grid sweep probe_window, probe_rate, and probe_backoff to find stable operating envelope.
Run on both x86 A100 and Ampere-L variants to rule out HW-specific kernel performance inversion.

root_cause_summary: Kernel-selector probes introduced a race between probing logic and KV-cache affinity updates. When request stream mixes short and long sequences, two kernels have similar cost profiles; the selector oscillates because probe scoring lacks damping and does not account for KV-cache residency impact, leading to cache churn and tail latency amplification.
mitigations_applied: Hotfix: rolled back aggressive probe window defaults in canary (config change).
Feature-flagged selector damping patch to add exponential backoff on kernel flips (PR in links).
Added temporary heuristic: prefer previous kernel if cache_hit_ratio < 0.7 to avoid evicting warmed entries.
